guidelineReference: Resus Council UK Acute Coronary Syndromes 2021
title: Cardiac chest pain in the stadium toilets
setting: Stadium toilets. Elderly patient feeling unwell, pale, cold, clammy, complaining of severe indigestion/chest pain that won't go away.
verdictExplanation: Severe central chest pain, respiratory distress, and profound cardiogenic shock (BP 70/40, pulse 120 bpm). Sick: call 999 immediately and treat.

shared.circulation: Very weak pulse, skin is pale, cold, and clammy

history.history: Suffering from severe indigestion all day, became dizzy and collapsed/sat down in toilets
history.additional: Friend found him and called for first aid

followUp.question: What does the blood pressure of 70/40 mmHg indicate in the context of this patient's severe central chest pain?

options.text: Profound cardiogenic shock; the heart is failing to pump effectively and the patient should be placed in the position of greatest comfort
A normal physiological response to severe pain; the patient must be sat upright in the 'W' position regardless of blood pressure
Hypovolaemic shock due to internal bleeding; administer an auto-injector immediately
A minor faint (syncope); help him stand up slowly and walk to the medical tent

followUp.explanation: With a BP of 70/40 and profound hypoxaemia (SpO2 85%), the patient is in cardiogenic shock with likely pulmonary edema. Laying them flat would acutely worsen respiratory distress. Keep the patient in the position of greatest comfort, call 999 immediately, and administer 300mg chewable aspirin.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Recognize cardiac symptoms, call 999. Treat for shock given pale/clammy signs (position of greatest comfort), administer aspirin 300mg chewable.
levelFlags.erNotes: Suspected myocardial infarction with cardiogenic shock (BP 70/40). Give high-flow oxygen, give aspirin 300mg. Position of comfort/flat. Monitor vitals, prepare AED, and expedite ambulance.
